newsitem.title: CHINA: China earthquake leaves 12 dead, 27 injured.
newsitem.headline: China earthquake leaves 12 dead, 27 injured.

text.p: Two major earthquakes rocked China's westernmost Xinjiang region within a minute of each other on Tuesday, killing at least 12 people, seriously injuring 27 and leaving several hundred homeless, officials said.

An earthquake measuring 6.4 on the open-ended Richter scale struck the Jiashi and Artux districts at 9.47 a.m. (0147 GMT), followed one minute later by a tremor measuring 6.3, an official of the State Seismological Bureau said.

"It was really terrifying, people could not even keep standing up, it was so powerful," one local resident said by telephone from Jiashi, about 50 km (30 miles) from the mainly Moslem bazaar town of Kashgar.

At least 12 people were killed and 27 seriously injured, state television said. Several hundred people had been left homeless after 500 houses collapsed and 1,000 homes were severely damaged in the Jiashi district, populated mainly by sheep herders and cotton farmers.
The number of casualties could rise as rescue teams and officials searched through rubble of collapsed houses, an official of the local seismological bureau said.
Dozens of aftershocks had rocked the region and many people were afraid to return to their homes, despite freezing temperatures, another official said.
Many residents had spread layers of cotton felt on the ground and had snuggled into it to keep warm, he said.
"It was a very strong earthquake," he said. "People are all very frightened, especially with the aftershocks which seem as if they will never stop. Some are big, some are small."
The seismological official said the first earthquake had measured at least 6.6 on the Richter scale.
"It felt much stronger than last time," he said, referring to an earthquake of 6.9 magnitude that rocked Jiashi in March last year, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
Unlike the March earthquake when officials had sent out warnings of an impending tremor, local residents had been taken by surprise on Tuesday, he said.
